title: One Sentence Each · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One Sentence Each · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose two players and a simple starting situation. The lead and partner alternate one sentence each until they have said four sentences. The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One Sentence Each, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The four sentences form one coherent story with an ending.
